general.title: General Settings
general.subtitle: Make OpenCode Mobile feel right for you.

welcome.summary: This app is a remote control for OpenCode running on your own computer.
details: Your computer does the real work: it runs the OpenCode server, the AI models and your project files.
Your phone connects to that server so you can chat with agents and follow their progress from anywhere.
The next steps take about a minute. Everything can be changed later in Settings.

permissions.summary: Optional: let the app notify you and listen to your voice.
details: Notifications tell you when an agent finishes a task while the app is in the background.
Voice input lets you speak prompts instead of typing them.
Nothing is requested until you tap Enable. You can skip both and turn them on later in Settings.

connect.summary: A server is the OpenCode server running on your computer. The app needs its address to reach your projects.
details: Scan QR code: pick this when your computer is showing a pairing code. It fills in everything for you.
Manual: pick this when you know the server URL, for example your https tunnel address, plus the username (usually opencode) and password.
Skip: continue without a server. You can add a connection later in Settings › Connection.

ai.summary: Choose which AI providers and models your server should use.
details: Providers (such as OpenAI or Anthropic) are configured on your OpenCode server; here you pick which ones to show.
You can skip this and keep the server's defaults.

project.summary: A project is a folder on your computer that OpenCode works in.
details: Pick the project to open first. Chats and file changes are kept per project.
Add a folder by entering its path on the server computer, not on your phone.

general.summary: Choose the model new chats start with and how messages you send while the agent works are handled.
details: The default model is used for new chats. You can still switch models inside any chat.
Steer sends your message to the running agent right away; Queue waits until it finishes.
Skip to keep the server's defaults.

ready.summary: Here is a summary of what you set up. Check it, then start.
details: Tap Start coding to open the app.
Anything missing or wrong can be changed later in Settings. You can also rerun this setup from Settings › Setup assistant.

transcript.summary: This controls how much of the agent's work the chat transcript shows.
details: Every chat shows your messages and the assistant's replies. The options below add extra rows in between.
Extra rows start collapsed. Tap one to expand it.
Pick Basic if you're not sure. You can change it later in Settings › Appearance.

look.summary: Choose a language, font, text size and accent color. The preview above updates as you tap.
details: The preview is a sample chat, so you can see how real conversations will look.
Text size adds to your phone's own font size setting.
The accent color also suggests matching background colors for the next step.

background.summary: Pick the colors behind the app and how panels look on top of them.
details: Gradient presets set three matching colors in one tap. The highlight color changes only the brightest one.
Panel style changes cards and chat bubbles: Glass is see-through, Solid is opaque, Crisp has sharper corners, Compact fits more on screen.
Animated backgrounds and fine controls are in Settings › Appearance.

transcript.title: What the chat shows
transcript.subtitle: Choose how much detail appears in each conversation.
transcript.later: Change this anytime in Settings › Appearance › Transcript detail.

basic.title: Basic: just the conversation
basic.body: Shows only your messages and the assistant's replies. The cleanest view.
basic.example: Example: “Fix the login bug” → “Done. I updated auth.ts.”

reasoning.title: Reasoning: show the thinking
reasoning.body: Also shows the assistant's reasoning, its step-by-step thinking before it answers, as collapsed rows.
reasoning.example: Example: a “Thinking…” row you can expand to see why it chose a fix.

verbose.title: Verbose: show every action
verbose.body: Also shows each tool call, such as reading files, running commands and editing code, as collapsed rows. Best for following exactly what happened.

look.title: Look & feel
look.subtitle: Make the app yours. Everything below updates the preview live.
look.previewLabel: Live preview of a sample chat
look.later: Fine-tune themes, fonts, icons and more later in Settings › Appearance.

preview.user1: Can you add a dark mode toggle?
preview.assistant1: Sure. I'll add it to the settings screen.
preview.user2: Use the system setting by default.
preview.assistant2: Done. It follows the system unless you pick one.

background.title: Background & panels
background.subtitle: Pick a background gradient and a panel style. The preview updates live.
background.later: Animated backgrounds, presets and fine controls are in Settings › Appearance.

skinHints.glass: Glass: see-through, blurred panels that let the background show.
skinHints.solid: Solid: opaque panels for the best readability.
skinHints.crisp: Crisp: sharper corners and stronger borders.
skinHints.compact: Compact: tighter spacing so more fits on screen.
